title: The finite-energy boundary of a group
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: Functions of finite energy on the Cayley complex of a finitely presented group, and the boundary they give the group. The first lesson sets up the Cayley complex of a presentation with relators of length at most three, proves that cocycles are gradients, defines the Hilbert space of finite-energy gradients and its subspace generated by finitely supported functions, bounds the interaction of two level cuts, and, when the two spaces differ, constructs a function with connected level sides. The second lesson, for a one-ended Cayley graph, embeds the group in a cube by the translates of that function and by functions recording the components of boxes, and proves that the closure is a compact metric space in which the edges have square summable lengths, that its boundary is a continuum with more than one point, and that vertices near a boundary point are joined by paths near it. The third lesson proves that the group acts on this boundary as a convergence group, compares g and gp for a parabolic fixed point p, and shows that every orbit is dense when the group is torsion-free. The fourth lesson proves that the boundary has covering dimension at most one, and that its first Čech cohomology vanishes when every 1-cochain on the Cayley complex with finitely supported coboundary can be corrected by a finitely supported cochain; so under these assumptions the boundary is locally connected only if it has cut points. These are the first steps of OpenAI's proof (2026) of the Singer conjecture in dimension four outside the middle degree.
prerequisites: core course Functional Analysis (D20): closed subspaces of a Hilbert space, the Riesz representation theorem
core course Measure and Integration (D10): Tonelli's theorem, dominated convergence
free groups and presentations of groups
for the third lesson: the course Convergence groups (lesson Convergence actions and their elements)
for the fourth lesson: the course Continua, arcs and cut points, and covering dimension (Definition 2.1 of Covering dimension and finite trivializing covers)
the course proves every other fact it uses

checks.reading: Each proof was written out and re-read step by step on 11 Oct 2026 against Section 3 and Lemma found:gradient of OpenAI's preprint (library copy at commit adc7f124). Lesson 2 spells out the cases of degenerate cells in the count of components and the three properties of the small box in the proof of the path theorem. The exercises on Z, Z^2 and the free group were worked out by hand. Lesson 3 was written against Section 4 of the preprint; it adds a proof that a group with an infinite cyclic subgroup of finite index is not one-ended, and gives the constant 2 in the diameter bound. Lesson 4 was written against Section 5 of the preprint; it replaces Hausdorff measure by an elementary notion of length zero, states the cohomological hypothesis on the Cayley complex, works with any abelian coefficient group, and adds an exercise showing that the hypothesis fails for Z^2.
checks.layout: Measured in the staged pages at column widths 1100, 768, 543 and 375 px on 11 Oct 2026: 2,107 formulas in the four lessons, none wider than the column, no TeX errors.

open_obligations: The translation between assumption (C_k) of the fourth lesson and the vanishing of the group cohomology H^2(Gamma; k Gamma) is not proved in the programme; it belongs to a course on group cohomology with group-ring coefficients, which does not exist yet.
The link between D_0 != D and a positive first L^2-Betti number is not proved in the programme; it belongs to a course on L^2-invariants, which does not exist yet.
free_sources: OpenAI, The Singer conjecture in dimension four (OpenAI Math Release preprint, 25 Sep 2026), Sections 2 and 3
